rationale: Getty AAT 300053648 defines brocading as weft patterning that weaves raised patterns; related Getty AAT 300227780 defines brocading weft as a discontinuous supplementary weft. This substantiates the extra-weft clue and distinguishes brocade from 050’s weft-loop pile. Candidate cites the broader AAT brocading record.
sourceLocator: AAT 300053648, Note; related AAT 300227780 brocading weft Note (official Getty indexed record)

rationale: Candidate narrows the baseline generic marbling clue to Turkish Ebru. UAL identifies Ebru as Turkish/Iranian marbling, says paints go into a water bath and notes the bath size makes paint float; its guide cautions traditions vary. Independent Met verification specifically describes Turkish-tradition ebru with color floated on a viscous carrageenan bath and transferred to paper. Distinct from carved relief and intaglio printing options.
sourceLocator: UAL Ebru and marbling context, lines 299–309; corroborating Met source: https://www.metmuseum.org/de/perspectives/marbled-paper

rationale: V&A classifies linocut as relief printing, describes linoleum as the material replacing the wood block, and explains relief printing cuts away areas around the desired image leaving raised areas to ink. This distinguishes the lino matrix from woodcut and drypoint.
sourceLocator: Relief definition, lines 34–36; Linocut printing, lines 51–52

rationale: Met defines woodcut as a relief process printed from a raised wooden surface and says the image is made by cutting away everything except the lines or shapes to be printed. Candidate’s wood-block clue is distinct from 074’s linoleum and drypoint’s intaglio plate.
